body:
In the United States, the Food and Drug Administration, usually called the FDA, regulates e-cigarettes and other electronic nicotine delivery systems as tobacco products. That regulation shapes which products can be sold, how they are labelled and what sellers may say about them. This guide explains in plain language what the FDA's role is, what marketing authorization means, how availability can change, what warning statements must appear, why we make no health or regulatory-endorsement claims, how our own FDA disclaimer fits in and how to stay informed. It is general information, not legal advice. Laws change and differ by state and city, so check the rules where you live. Everything we sell is for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## The FDA's role
The FDA gained authority over e-cigarettes and other products that deliver nicotine under federal law, treating them as tobacco products. The agency sets standards for manufacturing, labelling and marketing, and it can take enforcement action against products and sellers that do not comply. It does not approve vaping products in the way that it approves medicines. When people say a product is FDA authorized, they mean that it has gone through a specific premarket review process, which is not the same as being endorsed.

## Marketing authorization
New tobacco products generally need FDA marketing authorization before they can be legally sold. The process is called premarket review, and a manufacturer submits an application showing that marketing the product would meet the legal standard. Only some vaping products have received authorization. Many products on the market have not, and enforcement actions against unauthorized products can change what retailers may sell. Whether a product has been authorized is a regulatory status, not a quality rating, and we do not claim that any product is authorized, approved or endorsed by the FDA.

## What this means for buyers
Availability can change quickly. Products you could buy last year may become restricted, and some states restrict sales to authorized products only. A product may be available in one place and not in another. That is one reason we cannot ship every product everywhere, and why we may cancel orders that cannot be delivered lawfully. Check your local rules before you order, and ask us if you are unsure. See [state and local vape laws explained](/blog/state-and-local-vape-laws-explained/) and [where we ship and where we do not](/blog/where-we-ship-and-where-we-do-not/).

## Warning statements
Packaging and advertising must carry the FDA nicotine warning: "WARNING: This product contains nicotine. Nicotine is an addictive chemical." The statement must be clear and prominent. You will see it on our site and on product packaging. The warning exists because nicotine is addictive, and it is a reminder that these products are for adults only. See [what the nicotine warning label means](/blog/what-the-nicotine-warning-label-means/).

## No health claims
We make no health or regulatory-endorsement claims about any product, and you should be cautious of any seller that does. Regulations restrict claims that a product carries health benefits, reduces risk or helps people stop using tobacco, unless the FDA has authorized such a claim. We do not describe any product as treating, preventing or curing any condition, and we do not suggest that any product is a substitute for medical advice. If you have questions about nicotine and your health, speak to a licensed healthcare professional.

## Why you may see "FDA" in different places
You may see the FDA mentioned in several places: on warning labels, in news about enforcement, in our disclaimer and in product pages that discuss compliance. Each has a different purpose. A warning label is a legal requirement. News about enforcement is about what the agency does. Our disclaimer explains our position. None of them implies that a particular product has been approved or endorsed.

## Our disclaimer
Our [FDA disclaimer](/fda-disclaimer/) page explains our position in detail. It states that statements on this site have not been evaluated by the FDA, that the products are for adults and that we make no health claims. If you have questions about a specific product, ask us via the [contact page](/contact/). We will tell you what we know, and we will not make claims we cannot support.

## What responsible sellers do
A responsible seller follows the law on age verification and delivery, labels products correctly, avoids unsupported health claims, complies with tax and licensing rules and is transparent about what it does and does not claim. When you evaluate a seller, look for those signs. Be wary of a seller that promises federal approval of a product, offers to skip age checks or makes medical claims.

## How to stay informed
Visit the FDA's tobacco products pages and your state's regulator for current lists and rules. News about enforcement and authorization changes regularly, and official sources are more reliable than social media. Also read [state and local vape laws explained](/blog/state-and-local-vape-laws-explained/) and [the PACT Act explained](/blog/pact-act-explained-for-vape-buyers/), which cover the rules for shipping and selling.

## Common questions
### Does "not evaluated by the FDA" mean the product is bad?
No. It is a standard statement that the agency has not evaluated the statements made about a product. It does not say anything positive or negative about the product itself.

### Can I check whether a product is authorized?
The FDA publishes information about authorized products on its website. Check there, and ask us if you want to know what we know about a listing.

### Why do some products disappear from sale?
Enforcement and regulatory changes can remove products from the market, and manufacturers also discontinue products. If a product you like is unavailable, check related products, and ask us.

### Do you sell authorized products only?
We make no claim that any product is authorized, approved or endorsed by the FDA. Availability depends on what manufacturers supply and what the law allows where you live.

### Does vaping carry health benefits?
We make no health claims. Nicotine is addictive, and these products are for adults aged 21 and over. If you have a health question, speak to a professional.

## Browse responsibly
Adults 21+ only. See [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/) when you are ready, and read [what 21+ age verification means](/blog/what-21-plus-age-verification-means/) and our [terms](/terms/).

## A short glossary
- **Premarket review:** the FDA process for deciding whether a new tobacco product may be marketed.
- **Marketing authorization:** the result of that process when it is favorable, which allows a specific product to be sold in the United States.
- **Enforcement action:** a step the agency takes against products or sellers that do not comply, such as warning letters or seizures.
- **Warning statement:** the required nicotine warning on packaging and advertising.
- **Unauthorized product:** one that has not received marketing authorization and may be subject to enforcement.

Knowing these terms makes news about regulation easier to follow, and it helps you judge claims that a seller makes.

## How regulation can affect your choices
If a product you use is affected by enforcement, it may become harder to find. If your state restricts sales to authorized products, your options narrow. If a flavor is restricted where you live, you may need a different flavor or a different product type. These changes are decided by regulators and legislators, not by sellers, and they can happen with little notice. The best response is to stay informed, check the rules where you live and ask us what is available.

## What we will and will not say about a product
We will tell you what we know about a listing: the brand, the flavor, the strength, the size and the specifications. We will not tell you that a product is authorized, approved or endorsed by the FDA, and we will not make claims about health benefits. If you ask a question that we cannot answer, we will say so, and we will point you to official sources. That approach protects you from misleading claims, and it is how a responsible seller behaves.

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Why does your site include a disclaimer?
Regulations restrict what sellers may say about these products, and a clear disclaimer helps you understand our position. It states that the statements on this site have not been evaluated by the FDA, that the products are for adults and that we make no health claims.

### Can I rely on product descriptions for medical decisions?
No. Descriptions explain what a product is and how it works. They are not medical advice, and they do not make health claims. Speak to a licensed healthcare professional about health questions.

### What should I do if I see a seller making health claims?
Be cautious. Claims that a product treats or prevents a condition, or carries no risk, are not supported and may not be lawful. Compare with sellers that explain products plainly and follow the rules.

### A note on language
Words matter in this area. We avoid terms such as approved, certified or endorsed when we describe products, because they suggest a level of regulatory review that we cannot claim. We describe what a product is, what it contains where the manufacturer lists it and how it is used. If you see stronger language elsewhere, check what it is based on. Plain descriptions and honest disclaimers are signs of a seller that takes the rules seriously.
